titleEn: Tie Your Vest, Then Climb Aboard!

pages.text: "I want to get on first!" Lolo in yellow boots splashed through a puddle and ran to the boat. Tied by its rope, the motorboat bobbed. Dad the fisherman quickly caught Lolo's shoulders.
"Today we get to sit in the boat too!" Lolo stamped eagerly. Dad brought out two orange life jackets. "Wear these before boarding." "Too tight! Cannot we just get on?" Lolo pushed a vest aside.
Dad put his own vest on first and tied each strap. "I wear one every day when I go to sea. Grown-ups wear them too." Riri in her yellow hat counted on her fingers. "Dad has one, two, three straps!"
Dad put vests on Riri and Lolo and tightened the last straps. "Look, I cannot lift my arms well!" Lolo raised both arms only to shoulder height. One yellow boot was already on the boat's edge.
On the wet edge, Lolo slipped and tipped sideways. Dad grabbed a shoulder strap and pulled Lolo upright. "Oh? Dad caught my vest!" Lolo clutched the vest with both hands.

Dad tapped the straps. "This is a handle for Dad to hold. It also keeps you floating if you fall in, like that red ball on the water." He added in a singsong voice, "Tie your vest, then climb aboard!"
This time, Lolo put on the vest alone, tying each strap firmly. Dad waited with an open palm. "Tie your vest, then climb aboard!" Lolo called happily.
All three sat along the boat's side. The rope stayed tied to the post. Though waves lifted and lowered the boat, Lolo was not scared. "The vest feels like a tight hug!"

The next day and the day after, Lolo looked for a vest first at the boat. One, vest on first! Two, tie all three straps! Three, hold Dad's hand to board! Riri touched Dad's vest. "Dad has three too! Tie your vest, then climb aboard!"

On the way home, Dad took off the vest and hugged Lolo tightly. Before going to sea, grown-ups and children put on vests first. "Dad, tomorrow I will put mine on first. Tie your vest, then climb aboard!"
